prompt:
Generate one single 16:9 frame from a gritty live-action historical film set in the Caribbean in the 1770s. This is an ENVIRONMENT SHOT: the weather and physical place are the subject. Natural photographic depth, ordinary imperfect exposure, humid surfaces, restrained color, slight organic grain. It must feel like a real place under weather, not a polished concept-art illustration or a tourist brochure. Authentic period materials: rough limewashed masonry, aged timber, wood shingles, small clay tiles, hemp rope, dirt or worn stone, tropical vegetation. No modern roads, concrete infrastructure, electricity poles, cars, engines, steel containers, corrugated sheet metal, rubber tyres, plastic, modern ships, modern roof sheeting, or visible cameras/aircraft. No fantasy castle, no pirate theme park, no oil-painting composition, no orange-and-teal grading, no gold light, no dramatic spotlight beams, no giant lightning bolt, no tornado, no tsunami, no fiery destruction. No caption, writing, logo, watermark graphic, split screen or collage. A continuous plausible space with useful physical details and a specific weather moment. This is a first frame for a restrained 10–12 second cinematic environmental shot; keep moving phenomena at a believable scale rather than frozen gigantic action.

A ground-based wide landscape view from a low earthen ridge just above a Caribbean SUGAR-CANE FIELD after the windstorm, not a drone view. The camera looks slightly downward across the first twenty meters of the field toward low tropical hills under a flat gray sky. In the foreground a rough muddy drainage ditch has overflowed and cut a small irregular channel through the field edge. Saturated earth and a few uprooted stalk roots are clearly visible. Much of the sugar cane beyond is flattened in broad uneven patches in the same prevailing wind direction, some green stalks remain leaning upright at the margins, torn long leaves stick to mud. This is a working 1770s agricultural landscape, not a pristine lawn or a row of ornamental palms. At far left edge only a sliver of an old limewashed shed and a broken wooden fence remains, no grand plantation mansion, no machinery, no modern irrigation, no wire fence or power poles. No central person. A single battered palm is cut by the top right edge and contributes an awkward foreground depth cue rather than a postcard silhouette. The storm has moved away; lingering gray drizzle is possible far across the hills but there is no heavy rain in the foreground. Quiet wet air, muted greens, brown runoff and pale overcast sky. The damage should read as disrupted work and livelihood, never as a spectacular apocalyptic panorama. Ordinary 32mm-equivalent lens and fixed viewpoint.
